terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. A long low hall whose front is an open colonnade and whose back is a solid wall, sheltering a 22 m gilded Buddha lying on its right side facing the colonnade, head propped on its right hand, left arm draped to the thigh and the legs stacked. A stepped stone platform steps down and out on one side as a forward apron; twelve square columns carry a shallow two-tier roof in terracotta tile with a gold border band and white bargeboards; the figure lies on its own low plinth with its soles turned down the length of the hall.

reasoning: The registry notes make an argument rather than a description: the figure is modelled as part of THIS asset and the long front is an open colonnade, because the two decisions depend on each other. A closed long low box has no recognisable feature at all and reads as a warehouse.
So this is a building AND a large statue, and its material budget has to cover both gold leaf and roofing. The figure is the only ORGANIC form in the whole kit.

Occlusion risk is the HIGHEST of the batch and scored 3: the identity of the prop is a figure seen THROUGH a colonnade, so every column is a chance to hide it, and the figure had to be reviewed from a straight-on side elevation rather than from the hero angle.
Action readiness is minimal: static landmark geometry, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The figure cannot be a box decomposition and cannot be a lathe. It is a long soft mass whose section changes at every point along it -- shoulder to waist to hip to calf -- which needs a station-by-station tube, and that is a shape helper written for this asset alone.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: a 22.5 m gilded figure lying on its RIGHT side facing the colonnade: torso taller than deep, legs one tall mass with a soft crease, left arm along the flank to the thigh
the head upright and tilted back, propped on the right hand with the elbow down on the plinth
the flame-topped cranial bump -- the single most identifying feature of a Buddha figure at any distance
squared-off stacked feet with a real toe comb, soles turned down the hall
twelve square columns leaving the whole long front open
gold border band along both eaves of both tiers
the platform steps down and out on +X as a forward terrace
white boards up each gable rake and along each eaves
black streaking on the lower platform courses, fading out by 1.75 m

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: The rear elevation is a solid wall, as the plate shows on the visible side. Whether the real building is colonnaded on both long sides cannot be known from one view and no proxy exists.

The figure's robe folds, the incised hairline, the facial features and the 108 auspicious marks on the soles are NOT authored. The figure carries its posture, its proportion, its ushnisha and its toe comb -- what reads through a colonnade at prop distance -- and nothing finer.

The figure is authored at 22.5 m within a 28 m hall. The registry notes say the figure alone sets the minimum length, and this is the proportion the plate shows, but with no reference mesh there is no independent check on it.

The interior is a solid mass with a dark face, not a room. This prop is an exterior shell even though its interior is what you look at -- what you look at is the FIGURE, and behind the figure a single dark panel does the work of a room.
The roof tiles are individually laid pantiles in the plate with a woven gold border; the model carries flat tile fields and a flat band.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 14.00 x 10.00 x 28.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=32000 triangles, <=24 draw calls, <=16 materials, <=32 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Static landmark geometry: nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and gets no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole envelope; a level builder collides with the hall, not with the figure inside it.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

assumptions: The rear elevation is a solid wall, as the plate shows on the visible side. Whether the real building is colonnaded on both long sides cannot be known from one view and no proxy exists.

The figure's robe folds, the incised hairline, the facial features and the 108 auspicious marks on the soles are NOT authored. The figure carries its posture, its proportion, its ushnisha and its toe comb -- what reads through a colonnade at prop distance -- and nothing finer.

The figure is authored at 22.5 m within a 28 m hall. The registry notes say the figure alone sets the minimum length, and this is the proportion the plate shows, but with no reference mesh there is no independent check on it.

The interior is a solid mass with a dark face, not a room. This prop is an exterior shell even though its interior is what you look at -- what you look at is the FIGURE, and behind the figure a single dark panel does the work of a room.
The roof tiles are individually laid pantiles in the plate with a woven gold border; the model carries flat tile fields and a flat band.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares, +Y up, long axis on Z, colonnade facing +X. The figure lies on its RIGHT side facing the colonnade, which puts its head at +Z and its feet at -Z (body up = right x forward = (-Y) x (+X) = +Z), so from the front the head is at the viewer's left as it is on the plate. The hall is NOT centred in x: it occupies the -X side of the platform and the forward apron takes the rest, which is why the roof is centred at x=-1.72 rather than on the origin -- a roof centred on the prop would overhang the wrong side and miss the colonnade entirely.

silhouette.description: A long stepped platform, a colonnade to 6.60 m, and a shallow two-tier roof to a ridge at 9.78 m. The prop is nearly three times as long as it is tall, and the silhouette events are the column rhythm, the two roof steps, and the forward apron breaking the platform outline on one side. The figure is not in the silhouette at all: it is seen only THROUGH the colonnade, which is exactly what the registry notes describe.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -7.01..+7.00 and z spans -14.00..+14.00, both set by the bottom platform slab; y spans 0.00 to 9.94, the ridge cap. The 0.01 m on -x is a bargeboard on the roof's far rake, and the roof is what had to be pulled in to get even that close: the boards sit at half-length plus 0.06 rather than plus 0.12, and the tiers came down from 5.25 and 13.90 to 5.15 and 13.80.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: THERE IS NO REFERENCE MESH FOR THIS ASSET, and it is the only one in the batch without one. Meshy's image-to-3d refused the plate with content_policy_violation -- almost certainly a false positive on the reclining figure -- so there is no proxy to render through the same browser route and no band-by-band proportional comparison to check against. Every other prop in this batch had its proportions corrected by that table, three of them substantially; this one has only the single plate, and its proportions are therefore the weakest-evidenced in the set. That is reported rather than worked around: the mesh is evidence and this prop is missing it.

viewEvidence.note: NOT OBSERVED, and the lowest confidence in the monumental set. The plate shows the colonnade elevation and one end; the back is a solid wall in the plate too, so its blankness is at least consistent -- but with no reference mesh there is nothing to check it against, and whether the far elevation is also colonnaded is unknowable.

componentTree.name: Interior shade
componentTree.topologyRationale: The dark the colonnade looks into: the back wall's inner face and the soffit above the figure. This prop is the one case in the batch where the INSIDE of a wall is genuinely seen, straight through the open front.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Two panels -- a wall face and a soffit -- filling the gaps between the columns.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Two shallow tiers from eaves at 6.60 to a ridge at 9.78, centred at x=-1.72.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Centred at x=-1.72 rather than on the origin, because the hall sits at the -X side of the platform; a roof centred on the prop would overhang the wrong side and miss the colonnade entirely. geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A gold band along the foot of both tiers.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Meets the tile field above it as an opposed butt at one height.

componentTree.name: Bargeboards and ridge
componentTree.topologyRationale: Eight rake boards, four eaves fascias and a ridge cap merged into one geometry.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A white board up each rake of each gable end, along each eaves, and a cap on the ridge.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The rake angle is atan2(RUN, RISE), not atan(pitch): rotateZ maps a box's +Y to (-sin, cos), so aiming it along the rake needs the COMPLEMENT of the pitch angle. At the ubosot's 46 degrees the two are three degrees apart and the error is invisible; at this hall's 33 degrees they are twenty-four apart and the boards stood off the roof like scaffolding.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: The same whitewashed stone as the platform and the columns.

componentTree.name: Reclining Buddha figure
componentTree.topologyRationale: Smooth-shaded station tubes -- ONE body from neck to ankle with no hip joint to show a seam, a ridge riding it for the upper leg, a left arm along the flank -- plus an ellipsoid head, tapered cylinders for the right arm and boxed hands, feet and toes, all merged into ONE geometry on the gold material. A reclining body is a long soft mass whose section changes at every point along it, and a box decomposition of that is not a low-poly body but a pile of luggage; and a single symmetric tube has no side, which is why the first build read as lying on its back. The only organic form in the kit.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 22.5 m figure lying on its RIGHT side facing +X, head at z=+10.6 and soles at z=-11.3: torso taller than deep, the legs one tall mass with the upper leg a ridge on it, stacked feet, the head upright on the right hand with the elbow on the plinth, the left arm lying along the top of the flank to the thigh, an ushnisha, long ear lobes and a toe comb.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Every station's centre height is DERIVED from its own radius -- cy = plinth top + ry, computed rather than authored -- which is the only way a varying section can rest on a flat plinth at every point rather than intersecting it or floating over it.

evidence: This is the largest deliberate deviation on the prop and the whole reasoning is recorded. The figure is the ONE surface in this plate that is never directly lit: it lies in the deep shade of its own colonnade, behind columns, under a soffit. Its mean gilt value across 41,296 warm-hued pixels is #7D6040 and a mid-flank crop is #674D2F -- both illumination rather than albedo, and both of which render the figure BROWN under three directional lights.

The albedo taken is the brightest QUARTILE of those pixels, #AC8E6F: the least-shadowed sample of the surface rather than its average. Every other material on this prop is measured on a lit face; this is the same rule applied to a surface that has no lit face. The brightest 8% at #BEA07E was tried first and rendered cream.

Shipped at #AC7741: that measurement's hue (30.5 degrees) and value (0.675) kept exactly, with the chroma raised from 0.36 to 0.62. The gilt is genuinely worn, the plate reads it in shade, and the harness drains what chroma survives -- and "a long tan mass lying in a hall" is not the asset the registry notes describe. Hue and value are the measurement; saturation is the correction.

Metalness 0.15, HALF what the rest of this batch's gilding carries. With no environment map a metal's specular has nothing to reflect and its diffuse is scaled by (1 - metalness), so a high value drains chroma out of exactly the surface that has to read as gold. This is the one prop where the figure IS the identity, so the trade goes the other way.

It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

repetitionSystems.name: Colonnade

placement.note: Eight along the open +X front at x=2.10, and two at each end at z=+-12.20.

repetitionSystems.rationale: Twelve columns at one geometry and one submission. The registry notes REQUIRE the long front to be an open colonnade rather than a wall, because a closed long low box has no recognisable feature at all.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: The capital block is sunk 0.15 m into the shaft so no two top faces share a plane inside the merged unit. Because these are instances, every one of the twelve is checked separately against every other component -- which is how a single soffit at the wrong height became twelve reported pairs.

AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.

featureReviews.evidence: A 15.1 m figure on its RIGHT side facing the colonnade, head at +Z: one smooth body from neck to ankle, taller than deep, the upper leg a soft ridge on it, stacked feet with a toe comb, an upright tilted head with ushnisha and ear lobes cupped in the right hand, the forearm near-vertical from an elbow on the plinth, the left arm along the flank to a hand on the thigh.
featureReviews.notes: The only organic form in the kit, and it needed a shape helper written for it alone: a reclining body is a long soft mass whose section changes at every point along it, and a box decomposition of that is not a low-poly body but a pile of luggage. Every station's centre height is DERIVED from its own radius -- cy = plinth top + ry, computed rather than authored -- which is the only way a varying section can rest on a flat plinth at every point. The first promoted build was ONE symmetric tube from head to feet with the head at -Z, and it read as a figure on its back facing the wall; the rebuild carries the asymmetry that says on-its-side. Two earlier pose faults were found by review rather than by a gate: the arm ran too high and too far and covered the head entirely from the +X side, which is the only side anyone sees this prop from, and the ushnisha wanted 0.70 m of height where the soffit leaves 0.50. Reproportioned with the hall: it keeps the hall's own z scale and THICKENS -- 22.04 m of head-to-toe extent to 15.14 m and the section from 2.80 to 3.08 m, so length/depth goes 7.2 -> 4.9, which is what a human lying on its side actually measures and 7.2 is a pipe. The factor must be SZ and not something chosen to fill the hall: the figure does not sit in the hall, it sits on the PLINTH, which is scaled by SZ, and one build at 0.79 put the feet 1.1 m past the end of their own plinth and out through the end colonnade.

featureReviews.evidence: Twelve columns leaving the whole long front open, with the figure legible through them along its length and a dark interior face at luma 82 behind.
featureReviews.notes: The registry notes require this and give the reason: a closed long low box has no recognisable feature at all and reads as a warehouse. The interior shade fills the gaps between twelve columns, so its luma margin over the backdrop's 58 matters more here than anywhere -- at the backdrop value the gate would read eleven separate holes through the building. Its two panels also had to drop from 6.60 to 6.54: at the column head height each shared that plane with every column, and because the columns are an InstancedMesh, check-coplanar reported one mistake as twelve pairs.

featureReviews.evidence: Two HIPPED tiers at pitch 0.64 -- about 33 degrees -- sloping in on all four sides from eaves at 6.60 to a ridge at 9.68, each tier carrying an ochre eaves course under a red tile field, a capped rib down every one of its four hips and a capped ridge; the upper tier's eaves overhang the lower roof's surface by 0.25 m to make the double eave.
featureReviews.notes: This was a GABLE and it was the largest single error on the prop. Cropping the plate's roof out settles it in one look -- both tiers slope in at the ends, every corner wears a white-grey capped diagonal rib, and the ridge is a short capped line well inside the eaves -- and both proxies agree: the reference end elevation narrows steadily from eaves to ridge, which a gable cannot do. Built now through the preamble's hipRoof at curveExp 1, a straight Thai hip rather than a temple sweep, with ridgeHalfZ = hz - hx so the pitch is equal along both axes -- which is what a hip IS -- and y1 derived as y0 + pitch * hx so the pitch stays the one that was measured. Two cones per tier carry the banding: the gold cone is the whole tier, the red field starts one band up and stands 40 mm PROUD, because flush they would be coincident co-facing surfaces over the whole roof and inset the red would never be seen. The ribs are chained along hipRoof's own parametrisation, not aimed straight: the helper flares its eaves ring by 1 + 0.045 across the lower third whether or not cornerLift is zero, so the hip bows and a straight box cuts the chord and lifts off the surface at the eaves. The old bargeboard rake-angle bug -- atan(pitch) where atan2(run, rise) was wanted -- is gone with the bargeboards, which were rake boards for a form this prop does not have.

featureReviews.evidence: Five materials at PBR confidence 0.822-0.860, four measured on lit faces and the fifth corrected with its reasoning recorded.
featureReviews.notes: The gilt is the largest deliberate deviation on the prop. The figure is the ONE surface in this plate that is never directly lit -- deep shade, behind columns, under a soffit -- so its mean across 41,296 warm-hued pixels, #7D6040, is illumination and not albedo, and renders the figure brown. The albedo taken is the brightest QUARTILE of those pixels, #AC8E6F, which is the same 'measure a lit face' rule applied to a surface that has no lit face; the brightest 8% at #BEA07E was tried first and rendered cream. It ships at #AC7741: that hue and value kept exactly, chroma raised from 0.36 to 0.62, with metalness halved to 0.15 because a metal with no environment map has its diffuse scaled by (1-metalness) and drains the chroma out of exactly the surface that has to read as gold.

reviewHistory.summary: ENVELOPE CORRECTED AGAINST A PROXY THIS PROP HAD NEVER HAD. Meshy refuses this plate, so the silhouette layer had been carried at 0.72 with nothing behind it. fal-ai/trellis and fal-ai/hunyuan3d/v2 both accept it: they read length/height 1.852 and 2.020 and width/height 1.226 and 1.265, agreeing with each other to 8.7% and 3.2% and disagreeing with the build by 46% and 13%. Height is the anchor and does not move -- the proxy END elevation puts the roof at 31% of total height against this build's 32%, so the vertical breakdown was already right. Plan scaled by SX 0.883 and SZ 0.687 to 12.38 x 10.00 x 19.24 m. Band table mean |delta depth| 0.7267 -> 0.0789, |delta width| 0.1312 -> 0.0739. The plate cannot arbitrate this and that is measured, not assumed: fitting its ground silhouette gives four straight runs whose two must-be-parallel pairs differ in image slope by 47% and 34%, so no single camera projects it and a projective solve is unavailable on this asset.

ROOF REBUILT FROM A GABLE TO A HIP, which is what the plate has and what both proxies show -- the reference end elevation narrows steadily from eaves to ridge, which a gable cannot do. Two hipped tiers through the preamble's hipRoof at curveExp 1 (a straight Thai hip, not a temple sweep) with ridgeHalfZ = hz - hx so the pitch is equal along both axes, the upper tier a second full hip whose eaves overhang the lower cone by 0.25 m to make the double eave. Each tier is TWO cones so the plate's ochre eaves course reads: the gold cone is the whole tier and the red field starts one band up and stands 40 mm proud, because built flush they would be coincident co-facing surfaces over the entire roof. The bargeboards are gone -- they were rake boards for a form that no longer exists -- and are replaced by capped hip ribs and ridge caps. The ribs are CHAINED ALONG hipRoof's own parametrisation rather than aimed straight from ridge to eave corner: that helper flares its eaves ring by 1 + 0.045 over the lower third whether or not cornerLift is zero, so the corner path bows and a single box cuts its chord and leaves the surface exactly at the eaves, where it is most visible.

FIGURE REPROPORTIONED. It keeps the hall's own z scale and thickens: 22.04 m head-to-toe to 15.14 m, section 2.80 -> 3.08 m, length/depth 7.2 -> 4.9, which is what a human lying on its side measures and part of why the old render read as a smooth pipe. fz must be SZ and one build had it at 0.79 on the reasoning that a uniformly shrunk figure would rattle around the hall -- wrong twice: it compared the TORSO span rather than the full head-to-toe extent, and the figure does not sit in the hall, it sits on the PLINTH, which is scaled by SZ. At 0.79 the feet ran 1.1 m past the end of their own plinth and out through the end colonnade.

reviewHistory.summary: Structural pass: the hall placed at the -X side of the platform with the forward apron taking the rest, the roof re-centred on the hall rather than on the prop, and the interior expressed as two dark panels rather than as a room.

Pose rebuild against the plate: the promoted figure was one symmetric tube with the head at -Z and read as lying on its back. Rebuilt on its RIGHT side facing the colonnade (head at +Z, up = right x forward): ONE body tube from neck to ankle, taller than deep, with the upper leg a ridge riding it -- a second full leg tube showed a step and a crease wherever it emerged from the hip; right arm a short upper arm to an elbow on the plinth and a near-vertical forearm to a hand cupped at the cheek, as the plate has it; left arm along the top of the flank to a hand on the thigh; head an ellipsoid tilted back with ushnisha, ear lobes and nose. tubeAlong made INDEXED so the body shades smooth instead of showing every station as a crease. One geometry, one draw call, 1,508 -> 2,308 triangles.

reviewHistory.summary: Surface pass: surface character is geometry and colour -- the figure's varying section, the toe comb, the gold eaves border, the column rhythm -- plus one delivered per-vertex streak gradient on the platform. No texture sets and no canvas.

Lighting pass: this plate is the darkest in the batch and its subject sits in its own shade, which is what forced the gilt correction. No rim light and no contact shadow; both recorded absent. Exposure 1.0, ACES filmic.
Interaction pass: ONE pivot (root, base-center), ZERO sockets, one BOX collider matching the declaration, no destruction groups matching the empty declared list.

featureReviews.evidence: A 15.1 m figure on its RIGHT side facing the colonnade, head at +Z: one smooth body from neck to ankle, taller than deep, the upper leg a soft ridge on it, stacked feet with a toe comb, an upright tilted head with ushnisha and ear lobes cupped in the right hand, the forearm near-vertical from an elbow on the plinth, the left arm along the flank to a hand on the thigh.
featureReviews.notes: The only organic form in the kit, and it needed a shape helper written for it alone: a reclining body is a long soft mass whose section changes at every point along it, and a box decomposition of that is not a low-poly body but a pile of luggage. Every station's centre height is DERIVED from its own radius -- cy = plinth top + ry, computed rather than authored -- which is the only way a varying section can rest on a flat plinth at every point. The first promoted build was ONE symmetric tube from head to feet with the head at -Z, and it read as a figure on its back facing the wall; the rebuild carries the asymmetry that says on-its-side. Two earlier pose faults were found by review rather than by a gate: the arm ran too high and too far and covered the head entirely from the +X side, which is the only side anyone sees this prop from, and the ushnisha wanted 0.70 m of height where the soffit leaves 0.50. Reproportioned with the hall: it keeps the hall's own z scale and THICKENS -- 22.04 m of head-to-toe extent to 15.14 m and the section from 2.80 to 3.08 m, so length/depth goes 7.2 -> 4.9, which is what a human lying on its side actually measures and 7.2 is a pipe. The factor must be SZ and not something chosen to fill the hall: the figure does not sit in the hall, it sits on the PLINTH, which is scaled by SZ, and one build at 0.79 put the feet 1.1 m past the end of their own plinth and out through the end colonnade.

featureReviews.evidence: Twelve columns leaving the whole long front open, with the figure legible through them along its length and a dark interior face at luma 82 behind.
featureReviews.notes: The registry notes require this and give the reason: a closed long low box has no recognisable feature at all and reads as a warehouse. The interior shade fills the gaps between twelve columns, so its luma margin over the backdrop's 58 matters more here than anywhere -- at the backdrop value the gate would read eleven separate holes through the building. Its two panels also had to drop from 6.60 to 6.54: at the column head height each shared that plane with every column, and because the columns are an InstancedMesh, check-coplanar reported one mistake as twelve pairs.

featureReviews.evidence: Two HIPPED tiers at pitch 0.64 -- about 33 degrees -- sloping in on all four sides from eaves at 6.60 to a ridge at 9.68, each tier carrying an ochre eaves course under a red tile field, a capped rib down every one of its four hips and a capped ridge; the upper tier's eaves overhang the lower roof's surface by 0.25 m to make the double eave.
featureReviews.notes: This was a GABLE and it was the largest single error on the prop. Cropping the plate's roof out settles it in one look -- both tiers slope in at the ends, every corner wears a white-grey capped diagonal rib, and the ridge is a short capped line well inside the eaves -- and both proxies agree: the reference end elevation narrows steadily from eaves to ridge, which a gable cannot do. Built now through the preamble's hipRoof at curveExp 1, a straight Thai hip rather than a temple sweep, with ridgeHalfZ = hz - hx so the pitch is equal along both axes -- which is what a hip IS -- and y1 derived as y0 + pitch * hx so the pitch stays the one that was measured. Two cones per tier carry the banding: the gold cone is the whole tier, the red field starts one band up and stands 40 mm PROUD, because flush they would be coincident co-facing surfaces over the whole roof and inset the red would never be seen. The ribs are chained along hipRoof's own parametrisation, not aimed straight: the helper flares its eaves ring by 1 + 0.045 across the lower third whether or not cornerLift is zero, so the hip bows and a straight box cuts the chord and lifts off the surface at the eaves. The old bargeboard rake-angle bug -- atan(pitch) where atan2(run, rise) was wanted -- is gone with the bargeboards, which were rake boards for a form this prop does not have.

featureReviews.evidence: Five materials at PBR confidence 0.822-0.860, four measured on lit faces and the fifth corrected with its reasoning recorded.
featureReviews.notes: The gilt is the largest deliberate deviation on the prop. The figure is the ONE surface in this plate that is never directly lit -- deep shade, behind columns, under a soffit -- so its mean across 41,296 warm-hued pixels, #7D6040, is illumination and not albedo, and renders the figure brown. The albedo taken is the brightest QUARTILE of those pixels, #AC8E6F, which is the same 'measure a lit face' rule applied to a surface that has no lit face; the brightest 8% at #BEA07E was tried first and rendered cream. It ships at #AC7741: that hue and value kept exactly, chroma raised from 0.36 to 0.62, with metalness halved to 0.15 because a metal with no environment map has its diffuse scaled by (1-metalness) and drains the chroma out of exactly the surface that has to read as gold.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.86, up from 0.79, and the whole of the gain is that this prop finally HAS a proxy. Meshy still refuses the plate (content_policy_violation, safety checker forced on), but fal-ai/trellis and fal-ai/hunyuan3d/v2 both accept it, and two independent reconstructions agreeing is better evidence than one Meshy mesh. They put length/height at 1.852 and 2.020 against the build's 2.818 -- the hall was 46% too long -- and width/height at 1.226 and 1.265 against 1.410. Corrected to 12.38 x 10.00 x 19.24 m, the band table goes from mean |delta depth| 0.7267 to 0.0789 and |delta width| 0.1312 to 0.0739, with the bands over the 0.12 flag dropping from ten of ten to two. The roof was also the WRONG FORM: a gable, where the plate and both proxies show a hip. The remaining drag is materialSurface 0.82 and lightingCamera 0.80, and neither has an evidence-backed fix -- the plate is the darkest in the kit and its subject sits in its own shade, and a tile texture is exactly the opt-in the textureless default exists to refuse at prop distance. 2,892/32,000 triangles, 8/24 draw calls, 5/16 materials, 8/32 unique geometries.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero4x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Seven components and one repetition system: 8 of 24, the lightest draw-call load of the monumental set. The stone material alone serves the platform, the plinth, the wall, the twelve columns and the bargeboards.

materials.note: stone covers five consumers; five materials of sixteen, eleven in hand. The registry notes warn that this asset's material budget has to cover both gold leaf and roofing, and at five of sixteen it is nowhere near troubled by that.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 2,308 of 32,000 -- the lightest prop in the batch. The figure is about 1,500 triangles across its tubes, head and boxes, and it is the whole identity of the asset. There is real headroom to refine it further; what stops that is evidence rather than budget, since the single plate shows the figure only through columns and in deep shade.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A station-by-station tube, two extruded roof prisms and boxes. The tube is the only organic form in the kit and was written for this asset alone: a reclining body is a long soft mass whose section changes at every point, which neither a lathe nor a stack of boxes can say.

One InstancedMesh system carries 12 of the prop's 31 discrete parts. It is also the source of a lesson: every instance is checked separately by check-coplanar, so one soffit at the wrong height reported as twelve pairs rather than one.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless and no canvas is generated at all. The individually laid pantiles, the woven gold border, the figure's robe folds and the 108 auspicious marks on its soles are what is lost, and all of them are below the resolvable band at the distance a 28 m hall is read from -- through a colonnade.

risks.description: This is the ONLY asset in the batch with no reference mesh. Meshy's image-to-3d refused the plate with content_policy_violation, almost certainly a false positive on the reclining figure, so there is no band-by-band comparison to check the proportions against.
risks.mitigation: None available, and that is the honest answer. Every other prop in this batch had its proportions corrected by that table and three of them substantially -- the prang's terrace, the khmer sanctuary's roof and the chinese shrine's whole orientation. This one has only the single plate, and its proportions are the weakest-evidenced in the set. Reported at high severity rather than buried, because the missing check is exactly the one that caught the largest errors elsewhere.

risks.description: The figure ships at #AC7741 against a measured #AC8E6F -- the same hue and value, with the chroma raised from 0.36 to 0.62.
risks.mitigation: The figure is the one surface in the plate that is never directly lit, so its measured chroma is a shade reading; the gilt is genuinely worn; and the harness drains what chroma survives. Shipped as measured it renders a pale tan, and that is not the asset the registry notes describe. Hue and value are the measurement, saturation is the correction, and the whole chain -- mean #7D6040, quartile #AC8E6F, shipped #AC7741 -- is recorded on the material.

risks.description: Robe folds, hairline, facial features and the sole markings are absent.
risks.mitigation: The figure carries posture, proportion, ushnisha and toe comb -- what reads through a colonnade at prop distance. The plate itself shows the figure only in shade behind columns, so it is thin evidence for finer work as well as a poor place to spend triangles.
